newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Signature sees more Australasian purchases in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Signature sees more Australasian purchases in 1997.

text.p: Signature Security Group expects to buy more Australasian electronics companies over the course of this year and to achieve A$100 million a year in sales within five years, Chief Executive Jim Covert said on Tuesday.
Covert told Reuters he expects to announce significant acquisitions soon.
"We are working on that right now. We would expect significant acquisitions, frankly, within the next 100 days. We would expect three or four more before the year is over," he said.

Signature, 80-percent owned by Canadian investment bank Clairvest Group Inc and 20 percent by Covert, earlier announced it had bought the electronic security assets of Securitas Ltd in New Zealand and of Tempo Services Ltd in Australia.
Securitas is owned by Australia's John Schaeffer, who is also chairman of Tempo.
Combined, the two operations have annual turnover of A$20 million.
Signature, the holding company for the Australasian joint venture, would be run by New Zealanders and Australians, with headquarters in Sydney.
The New Zealand operations will be known as Securitas Electronic Protection Services Ltd.
The joint venture would offer rental lease systems bundling together security services with the aim of making protection more affordable, thus replicating services available in the U.S.

"We would expect to be a A$100 million dollar business over the next five years and to have probably 1,000 employees between Australia and New Zealand (from 140 now) through acquisitions and internal growth," Covert said.

"It will all be in electronics...unless we don't have a choice. Here, we will probably run into some companies where we have to buy some manpower services, but it would our desire at that point to spin that off. We really want to concentrate and focus on electronics," he said.

"The electronics part of the business -- the alarm side of the business -- is really seen as a huge industry in the U.S. and Canada. Here, because we have so much manpower, it always seems to be seen as a division of something.

"Our real interest is in taking the electronics from as many companies as we can, combine them and turn it into an industry." Covert said the group would work with insurance companies to ensure people who had adequate security received discounts on their insurance policies.
"Therefore you can advertise the cost of the system just in the returns that you can get off your insurance policy."
Financing for the Securitas/Tempo transaction was done through Toronto-Dominion Australia.

Contrary to popular belief, there were more burglaries in Australia and New Zealand per 100,000 people than in the United States: in the U.S. there were 1,200 per 100,000 a year, Australia 2,200 and New Zealand 2,700, he said.

"Everybody thinks America has horrendous crime rates. Certainly we have more violent crime in North America but when you look at crimes of property - stolen vehicles and robberies and that kind of thing, you exceed us by quite a bit."
Covert started Securitylink in the U.S. after serving with the U.S. Secret Service under presidents Nixon, Ford and Carter, building it in seven years into the world's third largest alarm company.
Securitylink, then with revenue of more than US$250 million, was sold to Ameritech in 1994.

Securitylink provided electronic security protection for the U.S. Secret Service, the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Central Intelligence Agency. Covert said he still acts as a consultant for the Secret Service.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
